collection_name: Nepal Grade 11–12 Science Practice MCQs - Biology
subject: Biology
intended_use: Practice question bank for Nepal Grade 11 & 12 Biology

schema_notes.correct_options: Array of option keys; supports single- and multi-select answers
schema_notes.is_multi_select: True when more than one option is correct

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following are monosaccharides?
questions.explanation: Glucose, fructose and ribose are monosaccharides; sucrose is a disaccharide.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is the main site of aerobic ATP production in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria host the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, producing much of the ATP in aerobic eukaryotic cells.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which stage of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move toward opposite poles?
questions.explanation: During anaphase, sister chromatids separate and are pulled toward opposite poles.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which factors can limit the rate of photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Light, carbon dioxide, temperature and functional photosynthetic tissue can all limit photosynthesis depending on conditions.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: For a monohybrid cross Aa × Aa with complete dominance, what is the expected phenotypic ratio?
questions.explanation: The genotypic ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, producing a 3:1 dominant-to-recessive phenotypic ratio.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which features are characteristic of typical bacteria?

options.text: They always have a cellulose cell wall
Their cell wall commonly contains peptidoglycan

questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotic, have 70S ribosomes and commonly have peptidoglycan cell walls; cellulose walls are typical of plants, not bacteria.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a typical food chain, energy transfer between trophic levels is generally:

options.text: About 10% on average, though it varies

questions.explanation: The ecological 10% rule is a rough generalization; actual transfer efficiency varies across ecosystems and trophic levels.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which are functions of epithelial tissue?

options.text: Conduction of nerve impulses as its primary role

questions.explanation: Epithelial tissues commonly protect, absorb and secrete. Nerve impulse conduction is the primary role of nervous tissue.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DNA replication is described as semiconservative because each daughter DNA molecule contains:

options.text: One parental strand and one newly synthesized strand

questions.explanation: Each daughter DNA double helix retains one parental strand and includes one new strand.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which conditions can contribute to evolution by natural selection?

options.text: Differences in survival or reproductive success
Traits affecting fitness being passed to offspring

questions.explanation: Natural selection acts on heritable variation when individuals differ in reproductive success; genetic identity would remove the relevant variation.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In human lungs, most oxygen diffuses from alveoli into blood because:

options.text: Oxygen partial pressure is higher in alveolar air than in deoxygenated blood
Oxygen is actively pumped across the alveolar wall using ATP
The alveolar wall is thick and impermeable

questions.explanation: Oxygen diffuses down its partial-pressure gradient across the thin alveolar-capillary membrane.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormone lowers blood glucose concentration by promoting cellular glucose uptake and storage?
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake in responsive tissues and storage as glycogen, lowering blood glucose.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In humans, fertilization normally occurs in which part of the female reproductive tract?
questions.explanation: Fertilization most commonly occurs in the ampullary region of the uterine tube.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which components are required for a standard PCR reaction?
questions.explanation: PCR requires template DNA, primers, thermostable DNA polymerase, dNTPs and a suitable reaction buffer with Mg²⁺.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cells can differentiate into antibody-secreting plasma cells?
questions.explanation: Activated B lymphocytes can differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which factors can increase transpiration rate in many terrestrial plants, provided other factors are not limiting?

options.text: Higher temperature within a suitable range
Greater water availability to the roots

questions.explanation: Air movement removes the humid boundary layer; suitable warming can increase evaporation. High humidity usually reduces the water-vapour gradient, while adequate root water helps sustain transpiration.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which statements about viruses are generally correct?

options.text: They contain DNA or RNA as genetic material
They replicate independently on nutrient agar without host cells
They require host-cell machinery for replication
All viruses have both DNA and RNA genomes

questions.explanation: Viruses have DNA or RNA genomes and depend on host cells for replication; they do not all contain both types of nucleic acid.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which statements about translation are correct?

options.text: tRNA brings amino acids to the ribosome
A stop codon normally codes for an amino acid
The amino-acid sequence is assembled into a polypeptide

questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA codons, tRNAs deliver amino acids, and a polypeptide is assembled. Stop codons signal termination rather than coding for an amino acid.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB-style practice; verify against the current official syllabus.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is known as the "powerhouse of the cell" and contains its own circular DNA and S$ ribosomes?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate cellular ATP via oxidative phosphorylation and the Krebs cycle. They possess semiautonomous circular DNA and bacterial-like S$ ribosomes according to the endosymbiotic theory.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which phase of meiotic prophase I does crossing over (genetic recombination) occur between non-sister chromatids?
questions.explanation: In the pachytene stage of Prophase I, the recombinase enzyme complex mediates crossing over between non-sister chromatids of homologous chromosomes, producing genetic variation.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In $ photosynthetic plants, the primary $\text{CO}_2$ acceptor enzyme RuBisCO catalyzes the carboxylation of which 5-carbon sugar?
questions.explanation: RuBisCO carboxylates Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate (RuBP, 5C) to yield an unstable 6-carbon intermediate that immediately cleaves into two molecules of 3-phosphoglycerate (3-PGA, 3C).
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue lines the inner lumen of the fallopian tubes and bronchioles to propel fluids and mucus?
questions.explanation: Ciliated columnar epithelium possesses apical micro-cilia that beat rhythmically in coordinated waves to propel the ovum through the oviduct and clear inhaled dust particles from the airways.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the human digestive system, the acidic chime entering the duodenum stimulates enteroendocrine cells to release secretin, which triggers the pancreas to secrete:
questions.explanation: Secretin acts on pancreatic duct cells to stimulate copious secretion of watery bicarbonate ($\text{HCO}_3^-$) fluid that neutralizes gastric hydrochloric acid to optimize duodenal enzyme pH.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a classic Mendelian dihybrid cross between two heterozygous individuals ( \times RrYy$), what is the expected phenotypic ratio in the $ generation?
questions.explanation: By Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment, a dihybrid cross of two heterozygous individuals ($) yields 16 combinations resulting in a :3:3:1$ phenotypic ratio.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The presence of vestigial organs like the vermiform appendix, nictitating membrane, and wisdom teeth in humans provides direct evolutionary anatomical evidence of:
questions.explanation: Vestigial organs are rudimentary homologous structures that were fully functional in ancestral species but lost primary function due to gradual divergent evolution and common ancestry.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In recombinant DNA technology, the enzyme commonly known as "molecular scissors" that cleaves DNA at specific palindromic recognition sequences is:
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases (e.g. EcoRI, HindIII) recognize specific symmetrical palindromic DNA sequences and cleave phosphodiester bonds, generating sticky or blunt ends for gene cloning.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which diagnostic enzyme-linked assay is standardly utilized for initial screening detection of antibodies against the Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV)?
questions.explanation: ELISA is the primary screening immunoassay for detecting HIV antibodies. The Western blot or PCR assay is subsequently performed for definitive clinical confirmation.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Lindeman's 10% trophic efficiency rule, if primary producers fix ,000\text{ J}$ of solar energy into net primary productivity, how much energy is transferred to secondary carnivores (tertiary consumers)?
questions.explanation: Trophic level 1 (Producers): ,000\text{ J}$ $\to$ Trophic level 2 (Primary consumers/Herbivores): ,000\text{ J}$ (10%) $\to$ Trophic level 3 (Secondary consumers/Carnivores): \text{ J}$ (10%) $\to$ Trophic level 4 (Tertiary consumers): \text{ J}$ (10%).
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In human females, the surge of which anterior pituitary gonadotropin hormone directly triggers ovulation from the mature Graafian follicle?
questions.explanation: Around day 14 of the ovarian cycle, high circulating estrogen triggers a positive feedback peak release of Luteinizing Hormone ("LH Surge"), which induces rupture of the Graafian follicle and release of the secondary oocyte.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The Meselson–Stahl experiment demonstrated that DNA replication is:

questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which RNA carries amino acids to the ribosome?
questions.explanation: tRNA brings specific amino acids to the ribosome during translation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Who wrote 'On the Origin of Species'?
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin published it in 1859, proposing natural selection.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which enzymes cut DNA at specific recognition sequences?
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases act as molecular scissors in recombinant DNA technology.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Antibodies are produced by:
questions.explanation: Activated B cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ovulation is triggered by a surge of which hormone?
questions.explanation: A mid-cycle LH surge causes release of the ovum.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of chemicals is mainly responsible for ozone layer depletion?
questions.explanation: Chlorofluorocarbons release chlorine atoms that destroy ozone in the stratosphere.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP through aerobic respiration.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Where does photosynthesis take place in a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many chambers does a normal human heart have?
questions.explanation: The human heart has two atria and two ventricles.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the phenotypic ratio in the F₂ generation of a monohybrid cross showing complete dominance?
questions.explanation: The F₂ phenotypic ratio is 3 dominant : 1 recessive.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which nitrogenous base pairs with adenine in DNA?
questions.explanation: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine through two hydrogen bonds.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is the primary site of aerobic ATP production in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out major stages of aerobic respiration and oxidative phosphorylation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The fluid mosaic model describes the structure of the:
questions.explanation: The fluid mosaic model describes a phospholipid bilayer with embedded and associated proteins.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main function of an enzyme is to:

options.text: Be consumed as the main reactant

questions.explanation: Enzymes speed reactions by lowering activation energy without changing the equilibrium constant.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: For a cross Aa × Aa with complete dominance, what fraction of offspring is expected to be aa?
questions.explanation: The genotypic ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, so one-quarter is aa.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The oxygen released during oxygenic photosynthesis originates primarily from:
questions.explanation: During the light reactions, water is split and releases oxygen, electrons and protons.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Most transpiration in a typical leaf occurs through the:

options.text: Xylem vessels directly to the air

questions.explanation: Stomata provide the principal pathway for water vapour loss from most leaves.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a typical food chain, green plants are classified as:
questions.explanation: Green plants capture light energy and make organic compounds, forming the producer level of many ecosystems.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In binomial nomenclature, a scientific species name contains:
questions.explanation: A binomial species name consists of a genus name followed by a specific epithet.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Crossing over between homologous chromosomes normally occurs during:
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs during prophase I, especially the pachytene stage, and contributes to genetic variation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which blood component is chiefly responsible for oxygen transport?
questions.explanation: Haemoglobin in red blood cells binds and transports most oxygen in the blood.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Transcription is the process of synthesizing:

options.text: Protein directly from DNA without RNA

questions.explanation: RNA polymerase uses a DNA template to synthesize RNA during transcription.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During translation, the codons of mRNA are read by the:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes read mRNA codons and coordinate amino acid addition to a growing polypeptide chain.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Natural selection acts directly on:

options.text: Phenotypic variation affecting survival and reproduction
Only acquired characteristics that are never inherited
The future needs of an organism
Every individual equally, regardless of traits

questions.explanation: Heritable phenotypic differences can affect reproductive success, changing trait frequencies over generations.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The functional unit of the human kidney is the:
questions.explanation: Nephrons filter blood and modify the filtrate to produce urine and regulate water and solute balance.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hormone lowers blood glucose by promoting glucose uptake and storage?
questions.explanation: Insulin promotes glucose uptake in responsive tissues and supports glycogen synthesis, lowering blood glucose.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In humans, fertilization normally occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Fertilization normally takes place in the ampullary region of the uterine tube.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main purpose of polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is to:

options.text: Destroy all DNA in a sample

questions.explanation: PCR uses repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing and extension to amplify a target DNA sequence.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Energy transfer between trophic levels is generally inefficient because:

options.text: Energy is recycled completely in ecosystems
Organisms use energy for metabolism and lose energy as heat

questions.explanation: Much energy is used in biological processes and dissipated as heat, so only a fraction passes to the next trophic level.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Antibodies are produced by differentiated:
questions.explanation: Activated B cells can differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antigen-specific antibodies.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is primarily responsible for producing ATP during aerobic respiration?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration and oxidative phosphorylation in eukaryotic cells.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of bond links amino acids in a protein's primary structure?
questions.explanation: A peptide bond forms between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of another.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pigment is chiefly responsible for absorbing light energy for photosynthesis in green plants?
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll a is the principal photosynthetic pigment in oxygen-producing photosynthetic organisms.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a monohybrid cross Aa × Aa with complete dominance, what is the expected phenotypic ratio?
questions.explanation: The genotypic ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa, producing a 3 dominant-phenotype : 1 recessive-phenotype ratio.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organisms normally occupy the first trophic level in a terrestrial food chain?
questions.explanation: Producers such as green plants convert light energy into chemical energy and form the first trophic level.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood through the aortic valve into the aorta and systemic circulation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During which stage of mitosis do chromosomes align at the cell's equatorial plane?
questions.explanation: In metaphase, chromosomes align at the metaphase plate before sister chromatids separate during anaphase.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature is generally present in bacteria but absent from typical animal cells?
questions.explanation: Bacteria are prokaryotes whose DNA occupies a nucleoid region rather than a membrane-bound nucleus.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which plant tissue primarily transports water and mineral salts from the roots?
questions.explanation: Xylem transports water and dissolved minerals from roots toward the stems and leaves.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Natural selection most directly favors individuals that:

options.text: Have traits that improve reproductive success in their environment
Always have the largest body size

questions.explanation: Heritable traits that improve survival or reproductive success tend to become more common across generations.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which enzyme synthesizes new DNA strands by adding nucleotides during DNA replication?
questions.explanation: DNA polymerase adds complementary nucleotides to a growing DNA strand during replication.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the main role of restriction endonucleases in genetic engineering?

options.text: To cut DNA at specific recognition sequences

questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases recognize particular DNA sequences and cut DNA at or near those sites.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In humans, fertilization most commonly occurs in which part of the female reproductive tract?
questions.explanation: Human fertilization most commonly takes place in the ampullary region of the uterine tube.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cells differentiate into plasma cells that secrete antibodies?
questions.explanation: Activated B lymphocytes can differentiate into plasma cells that produce and secrete antibodies.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is the main site of aerobic cellular respiration in eukaryotic cells?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the major sites of aerobic respiration and ATP production in eukaryotic cells.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary role of an enzyme in a biochemical reaction is to:
questions.explanation: Enzymes catalyse biochemical reactions by providing pathways with lower activation energy without changing equilibrium constants.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Most transpiration in many terrestrial plants occurs through:
questions.explanation: Stomata are the principal route for water vapour loss from the leaves of many terrestrial plants.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygotes, complete dominance predicts what phenotypic ratio in the offspring?
questions.explanation: For Aa × Aa with complete dominance, the expected phenotypic ratio is three dominant to one recessive.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a typical food chain, green plants occupy the role of:
questions.explanation: Green plants capture light energy and manufacture organic matter, forming the producer level in food chains.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygenated blood into the systemic circulation?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle pumps oxygenated blood into the aorta for distribution to the body.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ultrafiltration of blood in the human kidney begins in the:
questions.explanation: Blood is filtered under pressure through the glomerular capillaries into Bowman's capsule.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Natural selection acts most directly on differences in organisms' that affect:

options.text: The number of chromosomes in every species equally

questions.explanation: Heritable traits that influence survival and reproductive success can become more common across generations.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The principal purpose of polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is to:

options.text: Destroy all DNA in a sample

questions.explanation: PCR uses repeated cycles of denaturation, primer annealing, and extension to amplify a target DNA sequence.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which branch of biology specifically investigates the structure, function, and behavior of cells?
questions.explanation: Cytology (cellular biology) is the specialized biological discipline studying the structural anatomy and physiological mechanisms of cells.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The maintenance of a stable internal physiological state despite environmental fluctuations is termed:
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the biological capacity of organisms to regulate internal equilibrium such as body temperature and pH.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the five-kingdom classification system proposed by R.H. Whittaker, unicellular prokaryotes are placed under Kingdom:
questions.explanation: Kingdom Monera includes all prokaryotic microorganisms lacking a membrane-bound nucleus, including eubacteria and archaebacteria.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In binomial nomenclature introduced by Carl Linnaeus, the scientific name consists of:
questions.explanation: Binomial nomenclature designates each species using two Latinized names: the capitalized Genus followed by the lowercase specific epithet.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A biodiversity hotspot is defined as a biogeographic region characterized by:

options.text: High endemic species richness under substantial habitat destruction threat
Extreme climatic cold and polar tundra biome
High density of domesticated monoculture crops

questions.explanation: Hotspots contain at least 1,500 species of vascular plants as endemics and have lost at least 70% of their primary native vegetation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which organelle is universally termed the "powerhouse of the cell" due to ATP synthesis?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate cellular chemical energy (ATP) through oxidative phosphorylation during aerobic cellular respiration.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The cell wall of fungi is primarily composed of which polymer?
questions.explanation: Fungal cell walls are composed of chitin, a long-chain nitrogenous polysaccharide polymer of N-acetylglucosamine.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which type of covalent bond links consecutive amino acids in a polypeptide chain?
questions.explanation: Peptide bonds form via condensation between the carboxyl group of one amino acid and the amino group of an adjacent amino acid.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which lipid constitutes the primary structural bilayer of eukaryotic plasma membranes?
questions.explanation: Phospholipids are amphipathic molecules whose hydrophilic phosphate heads and hydrophobic fatty acid tails assemble into the fundamental fluid bilayer.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: DNA replication during the eukaryotic cell cycle occurs exclusively during:
questions.explanation: The Synthesis (S) phase of interphase is specifically dedicated to genomic replication and duplication of chromosomes.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Crossing over and genetic recombination between homologous chromosomes occur in which meiotic stage?
questions.explanation: Crossing over occurs during the pachytene sub-stage of Prophase I, facilitated by the formation of the synaptonemal complex.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of plants is widely known as the "amphibians of the plant kingdom"?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes inhabit terrestrial land but strictly require external water for swimming flagellated antherozoids during fertilization.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In angiosperms, a modified underground stem specialized for food storage having nodes and internodes is a:
questions.explanation: Rhizomes (e.g. ginger) are modified horizontal subterranean stems with clear nodes, internodes, and scale leaves.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which complex vascular plant tissue conducts water and dissolved mineral ions upward from roots?
questions.explanation: Xylem tracheary elements (vessels and tracheids) conduct water and mineral nutrients unidirectionally from roots to aerial parts.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The loss of water in the form of water vapor from the aerial parts of living plants is termed:
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the evaporative loss of water primarily through open stomatal pores in plant leaves.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which mineral element forms the central metallic ion of the chlorophyll pigment molecule?
questions.explanation: A single magnesium ion ($Mg^{2+}$) occupies the central position of the porphyrin ring structure in all chlorophyll molecules.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Double fertilization is a unique diagnostic reproductive characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Angiosperms undergo double fertilization: one sperm fertilizes the egg to form a zygote ($2n$), and the other joins polar nuclei to produce endosperm ($3n$).
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which phylum includes triploblastic, coelomate animals possessing jointed appendages and an exoskeleton of chitin?
questions.explanation: Phylum Arthropoda constitutes the largest animal phylum, characterized by segmented bodies, jointed limbs, and a protective chitinous cuticular exoskeleton.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A symbiotic ecological interaction in which both interacting species mutually benefit is termed:
questions.explanation: Mutualism is an obligate or facultative symbiotic relationship in which both partner organisms derive mutual survival benefits.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.subtopic: Levels of organisation in the human body
questions.question: Which basic type of animal tissue forms protective surface coverings and line internal cavities?
questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue consists of tightly packed cellular sheets covering outer body surfaces and lining hollow visceral organs.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Structures having common embryonic origin and basic anatomical plan but performing different functions are:
questions.explanation: Homologous organs (e.g. human arm, bat wing, whale flipper) share homologous developmental origins reflecting common divergent ancestry.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The classic Miller-Urey experiment demonstrated abiotic synthesis of which biological molecules?
questions.explanation: Stanley Miller and Harold Urey stimulated primitive reducing atmospheric conditions ($	ext{CH}_4$, $	ext{NH}_3$, $	ext{H}_2$, $	ext{H}_2	ext{O}$) with electric discharge, forming simple amino acids.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 11 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Secondary growth in dicotyledonous plant stems is predominantly brought about by:
questions.explanation: Secondary thickening in dicots is driven by lateral meristematic cylinders: vascular cambium (secondary xylem/phloem) and phellogen (cork cambium).
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The primary carbon dioxide-fixing enzyme in C3 photosynthetic carbon assimilation is:
questions.explanation: Ribulose-1,5-bisphosphate carboxylase-oxygenase (RuBisCO) catalyzes carboxylation of RuBP in the stroma during the Calvin cycle.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In aerobic cellular respiration, the terminal electron acceptor in the mitochondrial electron transport chain is:
questions.explanation: Molecular oxygen ($O_2$) acts as the terminal electron acceptor at complex IV, combining with protons to form water ($H_2O$).
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The innermost protective nutritive layer surrounding the microsporangium in a developing anther is the:
questions.explanation: The tapetum is the innermost specialized cellular layer providing nutrients and sporopollenin precursors to developing microspores.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a standard monohybrid cross between heterozygous pea plants ($Tt \times Tt$), the expected phenotypic ratio is:
questions.explanation: According to Mendel's Law of Segregation, crossing two heterozygotes yields a 3:1 dominant to recessive phenotypic ratio.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which nitrogenous base is present in RNA molecules in place of thymine?
questions.explanation: RNA contains uracil (U), a pyrimidine base that pairs with adenine, instead of thymine (T) found in DNA.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Enzymes capable of cleaving DNA phosphodiester backbones at specific palindromic sequences are:
questions.explanation: Restriction endonucleases (molecular scissors) identify specific palindromic recognition sequences to generate blunt or sticky cohesive ends.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Lindeman's efficiency rule, what percentage of energy is transferred across trophic levels?
questions.explanation: Lindeman's 10% law dictates that roughly 10% of gross energy is incorporated into next-trophic biomass, with ~90% dissipated as respiratory heat.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which specialized contractile tissue in the human heart possesses intercalated discs and myogenic rhythm?
questions.explanation: Cardiac muscle features striated branching fibers linked by intercalated discs containing gap junctions, facilitating coordinated rhythmic contractions.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hydrochloric acid ($	ext{HCl}$) in the human stomach mucosa is secreted by which gastric gland cells?
questions.explanation: Oxyntic (parietal) cells in gastric pits secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor required for vitamin B12 absorption.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The structural and functional units of gas exchange in the human lungs are the:
questions.explanation: Pulmonary alveoli are thin-walled, highly vascularized microscopic sacs providing extensive surface area for passive diffusion of $O_2$ and $CO_2$.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which cardiac chamber initiates systemic circulation by pumping oxygenated blood into the aorta?
questions.explanation: The muscular left ventricle contracts forcefully during ventricular systole to eject oxygenated blood through the aortic semilunar valve into systemic circulation.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: What is the basic functional microscopic filtration unit of the mammalian kidney?
questions.explanation: The nephron is the microscopic functional unit consisting of renal corpuscle (glomerulus and Bowman capsule) and convoluted renal tubules.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The gap junction across which a nerve impulse is transmitted between two adjacent neurons is a:
questions.explanation: A synapse is the specialized junction through which electrical signals or neurotransmitter chemicals communicate impulses between neurons.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Insulin, which decreases blood glucose levels by facilitating cellular uptake, is secreted by:

options.text: Alpha cells of islets of Langerhans
Beta cells of islets of Langerhans

questions.explanation: Beta ($\beta$) cells of the pancreatic islets of Langerhans synthesize and release insulin in response to elevated blood glucose levels.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which tough fibrous connective tissue bands bind bones directly to other bones at movable joints?
questions.explanation: Ligaments are strong bands of dense regular fibrous connective tissue connecting articulating bones together at joint capsules.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the human female reproductive tract, fertilization of the ovum typically occurs in the:
questions.explanation: Fertilization normally takes place in the ampullary region of the oviduct (fallopian tube) when capacitated sperm meets the secondary oocyte.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The modern synthetic theory of evolution synthesizes Darwinian natural selection with:
questions.explanation: Modern Neo-Darwinism synthesizes natural selection with chromosomal mutations, genetic recombination, and mathematical population genetics.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Tuberculosis is a contagious chronic bacterial infectious disease caused by:
questions.explanation: Tuberculosis is an infectious acid-fast bacterial pathology caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis, primarily damaging pulmonary tissues.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR), used for rapid exponential amplification of specific DNA fragments, utilizes:
questions.explanation: Taq polymerase isolated from the thermophilic bacterium Thermus aquaticus maintains catalytic stability through high-temperature thermal cycling.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Organisms that carry and express functional foreign genes introduced through recombinant DNA technology are:
questions.explanation: Transgenic organisms (Genetically Modified Organisms) are engineered to integrate and stably express exogenous recombinant target genes.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.
